memories.text: AtlasPlugin final decision: exact-match first, then a unique literal prefix; ambiguity fails closed.
BeaconPlugin final decision: canonical lookup first, then bounded local fallback; missing identity stays missing.
CinderPlugin final decision: literal exact ID first, then unique-prefix resolution; wildcard characters stay literal.
DriftPlugin final decision: exact canonical key first, then one deterministic alias; multiple aliases are rejected.
EmberPlugin final decision: exact chunk identity first, then a unique short prefix; ambiguous matches are rejected.
FjordPlugin final decision: exact memory identity first, then one verified compatibility key; collisions are never guessed.
GrovePlugin final decision: direct lookup first, then one bounded fallback query; fallback never changes authority.
HarborPlugin final decision: exact project key first, then a unique normalized key; duplicates fail closed.
IndigoPlugin final decision: canonical ID first, then a unique literal prefix; fuzzy matching is disabled.
JuniperPlugin final decision: exact resolver first, then one deterministic compatibility path; unresolved stays missing.
KestrelPlugin final decision: exact identifier when present, otherwise one unique prefix; missing stays missing.
LumenPlugin final decision: canonical match first, then a unique bounded prefix; ambiguity returns an error.

AlderIndex selection rationale: it preserved deterministic lexical fallback during vector outages.
AlderIndex known limitation: multi-evidence questions can still miss one required evidence item at top3.
BirchIndex selection rationale: it bounded candidate generation while keeping the original query.
BirchIndex known limitation: extra query expansion can displace a useful original-query candidate.
CedarIndex selection rationale: it reused one canonical projection path instead of adding a second disclosure path.
CedarIndex known limitation: candidate generation can still miss evidence outside the bounded depth.
DuneIndex selection rationale: it improved ranking without changing candidate authority.
DuneIndex known limitation: ranking cannot recover evidence that never enters the candidate pool.
ElmIndex selection rationale: it kept exact identity semantics while allowing bounded compatibility.
ElmIndex known limitation: ambiguous context still needs a caller-supplied entity anchor.
FernIndex selection rationale: it preserved isolated Core and Engine ownership during retrieval.
FernIndex known limitation: isolated reads do not by themselves solve multi-hop evidence composition.
GlacierIndex selection rationale: it limited planner influence to candidate expansion.
GlacierIndex known limitation: query expansion adds latency and extra embedding or search calls.
HeathIndex selection rationale: it kept the serving budget fixed at top3.
HeathIndex known limitation: a fixed top3 budget cannot contain more than three independent evidence items.
IrisIndex selection rationale: it allowed explicit reranking with atomic control fallback.
IrisIndex known limitation: provider nondeterminism can change low-ranked membership.
JadeIndex selection rationale: it retained the original retrieval path when the experimental layer failed.
JadeIndex known limitation: fallback preserves correctness but can forfeit the experimental quality gain.
KnollIndex selection rationale: it reused existing vector fusion instead of introducing a new ranking stack.
KnollIndex known limitation: RRF fusion does not guarantee preservation of every original-query candidate.
LotusIndex selection rationale: it kept runtime authority separate from source implementation.
LotusIndex known limitation: the design does not authorize AutoRecall or deployment by itself.

memories.text: AmberRelay final compatibility decision: exact canonical identity first, then one verified legacy key; collisions return no result.
BerylRelay final compatibility decision: direct project binding first, then a unique normalized alias; ambiguous aliases fail closed.
CobaltRelay final compatibility decision: exact resolver first, then one bounded compatibility lookup; missing remains missing.
DeltaRelay final compatibility decision: canonical key first, then a single deterministic migration alias; multiple matches are rejected.
EcruRelay final compatibility decision: exact record identity first, then one verified short key; fuzzy matching stays disabled.
FlintRelay final compatibility decision: direct namespace lookup first, then a unique literal compatibility key; wildcard characters stay literal.
GarnetRelay final compatibility decision: canonical binding first, then one bounded legacy route; fallback never changes authorization.
HelixRelay final compatibility decision: exact component ID first, then a unique normalized compatibility ID; duplicates fail closed.
IonLedger selection rationale: it preserved deterministic original-query retrieval while adding bounded semantic expansion.
IonLedger remaining limitation: recovered candidates can still remain below the final top3 after reranking.
JasperLedger selection rationale: it kept candidate authority in retrieval instead of moving it into the planner.
JasperLedger remaining limitation: bounded expansion adds embedding and vector-search latency.
KryptonLedger selection rationale: it reused the canonical projection path instead of introducing a second memory representation.
KryptonLedger remaining limitation: multi-evidence questions can still lose one required item in the serving budget.
MicaLedger selection rationale: it kept provider-backed ranking behind an explicit bounded adapter.
MicaLedger remaining limitation: cross-encoder ranking cannot recover evidence that never enters the bounded pool.
NacreLedger selection rationale: it maintained physical Core and Engine separation during benchmark retrieval.
NacreLedger remaining limitation: underspecified context still depends on the caller supplying a reliable entity anchor.
OnyxLedger selection rationale: it preserved the fixed final serving budget while expanding only the candidate pool.
OnyxLedger remaining limitation: a fixed top3 budget cannot preserve every independently relevant evidence item.
PyriteLedger selection rationale: it allowed semantic recovery without granting the Hint hard-filter authority.
PyriteLedger remaining limitation: provider scoring can reorder low-ranked candidates even when candidate coverage improves.
SiennaLedger selection rationale: it kept failure fallback on the original retrieval path rather than inventing replacement evidence.
SiennaLedger remaining limitation: candidate expansion does not itself authorize AutoRecall, deployment, or disclosure.
